text: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed, and only the output weights are trained. Training involves using a small portion of the data to adjust the output weights to fit the desired output. Reservoirs are usually trained using random initialization and do not involve explicit learning of the weights within the reservoir itself.
